sdkBundles.description: Bundled @servicenow/sdk + @servicenow/glide for authoring Flow Designer flows, Playbooks, Script Includes, ACLs, REST Messages, Connection Aliases, and more declaratively in TypeScript.
sdkBundles.releaseSummary: Feature release over 4.12.0, including the unannounced 4.12.1/4.12.2 patches (telemetry only). Glide stays 27.0.5, Node stays >=20.18.0, and none of the command flags or output lines Nova reads changed. NEW: a DatabaseView API (sys_db_view; author from the type file, because the release-note example does not compile); playbook variants, a Go Back activity, isIdealPath branches, action overrides, image attachments and public playbooks; indexes on augmented tables; Flow endFlow inside Catch; `--timeout` (default 3600 s) on `download` and `transform`; a new `now-sdk query <table>` command; `auth --add --password-stdin` for non-interactive adds; and MFA code prompts for basic-auth logins in an interactive terminal only (agent sessions and Nova's checks have no terminal, so keep using OAuth on MFA instances). FIXED: OAuth installs no longer replay session cookies, and an upload the instance redirects now fails with 'The install request was redirected away from the upload endpoint… The app was not installed' instead of reporting success; generated email notifications accept $meta, so Nova's strip-notification-meta step retires itself; augmenting a table no longer resets its access flags; column hint/help/plural serialise correctly. Expect emission diffs on the first 4.13.0 rebuild (sys_db_object access flags, sys_documentation). VERIFIED on the bundled binary: `now-sdk --version` reports 4.13.0 (glide 27.0.5); `install --help` is unchanged from 4.12.0 (`--source`, `-r`, `-a/--auth`, `--async` default true, `--demoData`, `--skip-flow-activation`); `download --help` and `transform --help` list `--timeout`; `auth --help` lists `--print`/`--format` and `--password-stdin`. npm still tags 4.12.2 as `latest` and 4.13.0 as `next`; the bundle pins 4.13.0 exactly.

servers.description: Drive a real browser for ServiceNow UI work — flow validation, workspace probing, portal smoke, dashboard verification, playbook UI checks. Per-project Chromium profile preserves saved passwords, history, and any persistent cookies (incl. SN 'Remember me' sessions when ticked at login).

headed.label: Show browser window (headed mode)
headed.description: Headed mode lets you watch the automation. Disable for headless / CI.

screenshotsDir.label: Screenshots folder
screenshotsDir.description: Where Playwright saves screenshots. Path is relative to project root.

profileDir.label: Browser profile folder
profileDir.description: Persistent Chromium profile per project. Preserves saved passwords, history, localStorage, and any cookies the server flags as persistent. SN's default session cookie is session-only — tick 'Remember me' at login if you want auth to survive browser close. Per-project keeps SN instance sessions isolated. With 'Browser profile per session' on slots, this folder is the first session's profile; a second session at the same time uses '<folder>~s2', a third '~s3', and so on, each keeping its own sign-in.

profileMode.label: Browser profile per session
profileMode.description: slots: each session that runs at the same time gets its own browser profile, so two sessions in one project can both use the browser, and each profile keeps its own sign-in. When every slot is busy, a session gets a temporary browser (signed out, nothing saved). single: every session shares one profile, as before; a second session sees 'Browser is already in use'. isolated: every session starts signed out and nothing is saved to disk.

maxSlots.label: Browser profiles per project (slots mode)
maxSlots.description: How many sessions of one project can each have a saved browser profile at the same time. Each profile that has been used takes up to about 0.5 GB of disk. The Project Doctor lists them and can remove slots unused for 30 days.

actionTimeoutMs.label: Action timeout (ms)
actionTimeoutMs.description: Client-side timeout for each Playwright action (click, screenshot, etc.). Playwright's own default of 5000ms is often too tight for ServiceNow UIs on corporate networks - screenshots wait on webfonts that can stall at a proxy.

useCases: Building or validating Flow Designer flows
Workspace + UI Builder verification
Portal page + theme smoke
Dashboard / Performance Analytics visualisation review
Playbook UI validation

servers.description: Runtime bundle for Nova Recorder: narrated, annotated ServiceNow demo videos rendered from a project playbook (demos/<name>/demo.yaml) by the sn-demo-recorder skill. Ships ffmpeg 9.0.1 (gyan.dev release essentials build, GPL v3 - LICENSE and THIRD_PARTY.md included) plus the yaml parser the recorder tool needs. The browser comes from the Playwright catalog entry and narration from the platform's offline voice; no third-party service or key. Windows x64 (flat tarball, ffmpeg 9.0.1) and macOS Apple Silicon (tarballs.darwin-arm64: ffmpeg-static b6.1.1 static build, reports ffmpeg 6.0; libass, libx264, fontconfig present).
useCases: Recording a narrated, annotated demo of a ServiceNow feature from a plain-English brief
Dry-running a demo playbook against the instance and fixing concerns before recording
Re-voicing one segment in the Demos panel and re-rendering only that segment
Producing a handover script (script.md) with review frames per segment

servers.description: Lets Claude load, sign in to, navigate, screenshot and record the ServiceNow mobile apps (above all ServiceNow Agent) on an Android emulator. Nova downloads Google's Android SDK tools, emulator and a Google Play system image onto this machine (nothing from Google is bundled; you accept Google's SDK licence in Nova first), builds one base device that you sign in to Google on and install Agent into from the Play Store, then gives each project that enables Mobile its own copy of that device, signed in to the project's instance. Claude drives it through the Mobile MCP (nova-mobile over mobile-mcp). Needs Windows Hypervisor Platform on Windows; about 20 GB free disk.
useCases: Verifying a mobile applet, card, list or action in ServiceNow Agent after building it (sn-mobile-verify)
Screenshots and recordings of the Agent app for a demo or handover
Checking what a fulfiller sees on mobile for a record, without a physical phone

servers.description: Nova's Mobile MCP (nova-mobile): Claude's hands on the project's own Android device. Starts and stops the emulator (headless by default), lists what is on screen as a short filtered list (about 90% fewer tokens than the raw accessibility tree, refs kept), taps by ref only on the element Claude was shown, screenshots, and records MP4s to the project's screenshots/ folder. Pinned to the project's device: another project's device, and every call in a project without Mobile, is refused. One Claude session holds a device at a time. It stops the device automation it starts (mobilecli daemon, app_process, adb forwards) when the session ends. Installed and enabled by the Mobile (Android) runtime, not on its own. Bundles mobile-mcp 1.0.5 (Apache-2.0), mobilecli 1.0.13 (FSL-1.1-ALv2, terms included) and scrcpy 4.1 (Apache-2.0); nothing from Google or ServiceNow. Windows x64 now; the macOS Apple Silicon bundle follows the consultant Mac check.
useCases: Verifying a mobile applet, card, list or action in ServiceNow Agent after a build (sn-mobile-verify)
Reading list counts, tiles and empty states on Agent screens through the filtered element list
Screenshots and MP4 recordings of the Agent app for evidence, demos and handovers

servers.description: Official Atlassian Rovo remote MCP server - live Jira issue + Confluence page read/write under your own Atlassian sign-in (OAuth in-session, permissions follow your Atlassian roles). No install, no credentials stored by Nova: enable per project, then sign in once via /mcp (Claude) or codex mcp login (Codex). Lets sn-story-manager round-trip a live Jira backlog instead of exporting CSV.
useCases: Round-trip the project backlog to live Jira from sn-story-manager (CSV fallback retained)
Read acceptance criteria / comments from Jira issues during builds
Publish build notes or release summaries to Confluence pages
